article_title: Kutti AI: A Voice-First, Offline-Capable Learning Companion with Real-Time Struggle Detection for Visually-Impaired Children
citation: Kadharmoideen Fadurudeen. (2026). Kutti AI: A Voice-First, Offline-Capable Learning Companion with Real-Time Struggle Detection for Visually-Impaired Children. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22377
title: Kutti AI: a voice-first, offline-capable learning companion for visually-impaired children
description: Kutti AI is a cross-platform mobile application (React Native/Expo, TypeScript) in which "the entire learning loop—presenting a concept, posing a question, capturing the answer, detecting difficulty, and giving feedback—is conducted through speech". It uses on-device Whisper ASR, platform text-to-speech, and a PostgreSQL (Supabase) backend with row-level security, and is intended to be distributed free of charge. The prototype supports English and Tamil.
requirements: Every function must be reachable and completable through speech and audio feedback alone; visual elements must never be required (R1)
constraints: The prototype has not yet been evaluated with visually-impaired children under controlled conditions; reported results are qualitative and formative
target_learning_goals: curriculum concepts delivered through spoken conversation
examples: Built as a working prototype during the Half Baked hackathon, supporting English and Tamil
key_sources: Kadharmoideen Fadurudeen. (2026). Kutti AI: A Voice-First, Offline-Capable Learning Companion with Real-Time Struggle Detection for Visually-Impaired Children. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22377

article_title: An International Review of Assessment Tools for Teachers’ Professional Competence in Teaching Autistic Children
citation: Nick Gerrit Hasche, Charlotte Dignath, Sumeja Mustafi, Mareike Kunter. (2026). An International Review of Assessment Tools for Teachers' Professional Competence in Teaching Autistic Children. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10176-x
title: Kunter et al. (2013) model of teachers' professional competence adapted to autism-sensitive inclusive teaching
description: The review adopts the multidimensional model of teachers' professional competence by Kunter et al. (2013), which distinguishes psychologically distinct constructs — knowledge, beliefs, and motivation — as personal prerequisites for effective professional behavior, separate from observable practices. As adapted by Hasche et al. (2025), it specifies autism-relevant knowledge facets (knowledge about autism and about specific evidence-based practices) alongside inclusion-related beliefs and motivational orientations such as self-efficacy. The review states: "Due to its multidimensionality, this model provides a suitable framework to systematically describe the professional characteristics that enable teachers to successfully include autistic children in mainstream classrooms." The three aspects are treated as equally relevant and mutually influencing.
requirements: Instruments must distinguish the psychologically distinct constructs of knowledge, beliefs, and motivation, since interventions targeting each operate through different mechanisms
The model requires separating observable practices from the personal prerequisites that enable competent professional action
constraints: The self-regulation component of the original model could not be incorporated because no operationalizations linking it to inclusive teaching of autistic students were found
The three competence aspects influence each other as well as inclusion outcomes, so they are not independent
target_learners: Mainstream (regular education) teachers of autistic children
Special education teachers and other educational professionals included in some instrument samples
target_learning_goals: Teachers' professional competence for the inclusion of autistic children in mainstream classrooms: knowledge about autism and evidence-based practices, beliefs/attitudes toward inclusion, and motivational orientations such as self-efficacy
examples: The review classified all 52 included instruments by whether they assessed knowledge, beliefs, or motivation within this framework
key_sources: Nick Gerrit Hasche, Charlotte Dignath, Sumeja Mustafi, Mareike Kunter. (2026). An International Review of Assessment Tools for Teachers' Professional Competence in Teaching Autistic Children. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10176-x

article_title: Pedagogy at the Berlin Psychological Congress.
citation: Peters, W. (1912). Pedagogy at the Berlin Psychological Congress. The Journal of Educational Psychology, 3, 452-457. https://eric.ed.gov/?q=Pedagogy+at+the+Berlin+Psychological+Congress
title: Kupp's two-function theory of memory: perseveration and association with threefold psychic effects
description: A systematic survey of the characteristics of memory presented by Kupp at the Berlin congress. It posits two elementary functions of memory: "perseveration, or the tendency for an impression to persist in consciousness," and "association, or the connection between two or more impressions." Their psychic effects are threefold: revival of the experience, a mere increase in receptivity for this or a similar impression, and arousal of the consciousness of familiarity on repetition of this or a like impression. The report presents this as a classificatory framework for memory research of educational interest.
requirements: Memory phenomena are to be analyzed into the two elementary functions of perseveration and association as Kupp defines them.
target_learners: school learners studied in experimental pedagogy
target_learning_goals: retention and reproduction of learned material
examples: Presented as a systematic survey address at the congress, organizing memory phenomena into two elementary functions and three kinds of psychic effects.
key_sources: Peters, W. (1912). Pedagogy at the Berlin Psychological Congress. The Journal of Educational Psychology, 3, 452-457. https://eric.ed.gov/?q=Pedagogy+at+the+Berlin+Psychological+Congress

article_title: An evaluation of the effectiveness of instruction and audience reaction to programming an educational television station
citation: Evans, Richard I.; Roney, H. Burr; and McAdams, Walter J. (1955). An Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Instruction and Audience Reaction to Programming an Educational Television Station. Journal of Applied Psychology, 39, 277-79. https://eric.ed.gov
title: KUHT-TV educational television station of the University of Houston and its televised psychology and biology course sections
description: KUHT-TV is the University of Houston's educational TV station, evaluated for instructional effectiveness and audience reaction. The study enrolled "17 subjects were enrolled in a TV-lecture only (correspondence) section, 96 in a traditional campus lecture section, 30 in a section which had TV-lectures plus two campus discussion periods a week" in psychology, and matched traditional versus TV-plus-discussion sections in biology. An audience telephone questionnaire to 384 people measured viewing behavior and program preferences.
requirements: Television lecture delivery, with campus discussion periods added in one psychology section and in the biology TV section
constraints: The traditional psychology class completed the course before the two TV classes began to prevent contamination; there was no preliminary matching or tests for significant basic differences in the psychology course
target_learners: college students in elementary psychology and elementary biology courses
target_learning_goals: college-level elementary psychology and elementary biology achievement
examples: The biology course had only two sections, traditional campus and TV-lecture plus discussion meetings, matched for age, grade and sex
key_sources: Evans, Richard I.; Roney, H. Burr; and McAdams, Walter J. (1955). An Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Instruction and Audience Reaction to Programming an Educational Television Station. Journal of Applied Psychology, 39, 277-79. https://doi.org/10.1007/bf02718467

article_title: On the Efficiency of Text Production in Vocabulary Learning: An Empirical Study on Iranian GFL-Learners
citation: Nader Haghani & Samira Kiani. (2018). On the Efficiency of Text Production in Vocabulary Learning: An Empirical Study on Iranian GFL-Learners. Journal of Education and Learning, 7(3). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v7n3p176
title: Kühn's three-step model of vocabulary teaching (receptive, reflective, productive)
description: Kühn's (2000) three-step model holds that vocabulary exercises should proceed in three steps: "The first step is receptive vocabulary practice, which involves understanding and explaining words with different semantization techniques", followed by reflective practice (notation, gathering, linking, ordering of words) and productive practice, "which involves the use of the vocabulary in appropriate texts and situations". The model follows three principles: success measured by learner output, functional orientation toward writing and/or speaking competence, and textual orientation. The present study operationalizes its third step as text production and tests its retention effects.
requirements: Vocabulary work must be anchored in texts so lexical means can be observed in authentic usage contexts and used in learners' own text production
constraints: The article notes the model itself has not received much attention and is still in its infancy
target_learning_goals: writing and speaking competence in a foreign language
examples: The study implemented a lesson plan integrating the concept's three steps, with the experimental group producing a text at the end of the learning phase
key_sources: Nader Haghani & Samira Kiani. (2018). On the Efficiency of Text Production in Vocabulary Learning: An Empirical Study on Iranian GFL-Learners. Journal of Education and Learning, 7(3). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v7n3p176

article_title: Evaluating the Effect of Simulation-Based Handover Training and Its Predictors: A Quasiexperimental Study.
citation: Tan, Kexin, Pun, Jack. (2026). Evaluating the Effect of Simulation‑Based Handover Training and Its Predictors: A Quasiexperimental Study. Journal of Nursing Management. https://doi.org/10.1155/jonm/6626003
title: Kuhl's action control theory as a framework for deconstructing perceived handover competency
description: The article applies Kuhl's action control theory to explain how internal psychological factors shape perceived handover competency. The theory holds that "successful behavioral change requires not only selective motivation but also volitional control": selective motivation is operationalized as intention to initiate (IIH) and complete (ICH) handover, while volitional control is operationalized as resilience in handover (RH), which shields intention from distractions such as hierarchical pressure and interruptions. Perceptions of protocols (PP) completes the psychological infrastructure.
requirements: Measurement of IIH, ICH, RH, and PP as distinct constructs (17-item instrument grounded in the theory)
constraints: Applied in the specific context of nursing handover in Hong Kong's hierarchical clinical culture
key_sources: Tan, Kexin, Pun, Jack. (2026). Evaluating the Effect of Simulation‑Based Handover Training and Its Predictors: A Quasiexperimental Study. Journal of Nursing Management. https://doi.org/10.1155/jonm/6626003

article_title: Reaching proficiency in robotic liver surgery in two high-volume European HPB centers.
citation: van Dorst R. W. J. J., Rinkes I. H. M. Borel, Gilg S., Molenaar I. Q., Hagendoorn J., Sparrelid E. (2026). Reaching proficiency in robotic liver surgery in two high-volume European HPB centers. Journal of Robotic Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-026-03372-y
title: KUH structured training pathway for introducing surgeons to robotic liver surgery
description: A sequenced training pathway used at Karolinska University Hospital to introduce surgeons to robotic HPB surgery: "The initially introduced KUH surgeons took at least 30 h of simulator training, followed by the Surgeon-Led Procedure Training Series (TR 300, Intuitive Surgical) at the Orsi Academy (Melle, Belgium)." This was followed by case observations at UMCU and multiple rounds of on-site proctoring at KUH. Laparoscopic liver surgery experience of these surgeons was comparable to that of the UMCU surgeons.
requirements: Access to simulator training of at least 30 hours, a commercial procedure training series, case observation at an experienced center, and on-site proctoring
target_learners: Surgeons newly introduced to robotic liver surgery at KUH
target_learning_goals: Safe introduction of multiple surgeons as console surgeons in robotic liver surgery
examples: The pathway supported KUH's guided majority-adopter implementation starting October 2020, through which a broader spread of console and tableside surgeon roles was achieved than at UMCU
key_sources: van Dorst R. W. J. J., Rinkes I. H. M. Borel, Gilg S., Molenaar I. Q., Hagendoorn J., Sparrelid E. (2026). Reaching proficiency in robotic liver surgery in two high-volume European HPB centers. Journal of Robotic Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-026-03372-y
